meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').

examples.trans: First they were rude and insulting over there.
Let's start everything from the beginning.

examples.text: Мы танцевали. Сначала они там грубили, оскорбляли.
examples.trans: We were dancing. First they were rude and insulting over there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Show me your hands!
Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'palm of the hand' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And we start pressing down with the palm of the hand.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая ладошка.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new palm of the hand.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: When do I start?
The lesson starts at nine.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

давить.gloss: to press, to put pressure on

meanings.en: to press, to put pressure on
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to press, to put pressure on', paired with 'надавить'.

examples.text: Не надо мне сейчас на совесть давить.
examples.trans: Don't try to make me feel guilty now.
Don't pressure me!

examples.text: Не надо мне сейчас на совесть давить. Я тебе всё отработала на тех выборах.
examples.trans: Don't try to make me feel guilty now. I paid you back in full at that election.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'small knife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: With a knife we trim off the ends of the garlic.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый ножик.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new small knife.

отрезать.gloss: to cut off, to slice off

meanings.en: to cut off, to slice off
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'резать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to cut off, to slice off', paired with 'отрезать'.

examples.trans: Will you cut my ear off?
Cut me a slice of bread.

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что? Ты мне ухо отрежешь?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what? Will you cut my ear off?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'end piece (of a cucumber/loaf)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: With a knife we trim off the ends of the garlic.
I would like to get something to drink.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'garlic' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: With a knife we trim off the ends of the garlic.
We place this garlic right inside it.
The garlic is completely peeled.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.

examples.trans: I'm not taking the knife.
Chef, I didn't take it.
We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'bowl' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Now we take a mixing bowl.
We take a second bowl.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to put, to lay down', paired with 'положить'.

examples.trans: Wait, don't hang up!
Where do you put the keys?

examples.text: Постой, не клади трубку! У меня есть деловое предложение.
examples.trans: Wait, don't hang up! I have a business offer.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there, thither', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю! Хочешь, сейчас и тебя туда увезут?
examples.trans: I know! Do you want them to take you there too right now?
They put bad meat in there for you.
Let's go there together.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('second').

examples.trans: This is my second term.
The second lesson is hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to shake'.

examples.trans: And we shake it hard.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет трясти без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to shake without a reason.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('peeled, cleaned').

examples.trans: The garlic is completely peeled.

examples.text: Сегодня у шефа очень очищенный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: Today the chef is having a very peeled day at the restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

переводить.gloss: to transfer, to move; to translate

meanings.en: to transfer, to move; to translate
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'водить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to transfer, to move; to translate', paired with 'перевести'.

examples.trans: We're moving the project to Kaluga.
She is translating a book.

examples.text: Давайте так: два дня. Или мы переводим проект в Калугу.
examples.trans: Here's what we'll do: two days. Or we move the project to Kaluga.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.
Don't laugh at me.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to yell, to bellow', paired with 'заорать'.

examples.trans: Bellowing songs!
Stop yelling at me!

examples.text: О, это, Аркашенька, бывает очень часто. Песни орём!
examples.trans: Oh, that happens very often, Arkashenka. Bellowing songs!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спрашивать'.

examples.text: А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Ask him where he put the computer lab.
May I ask you something?

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Really? Then ask him where he put the computer lab.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Me too.
He's here too.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('wonderful, miraculous').

examples.trans: This is wonderful caviar.
Listen, this is wonderful caviar!

examples.text: Какой чудесный и невероятно красивый город!
examples.trans: What a wonderful and incredibly beautiful city!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'литка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'snail, escargot' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Wonderful snails.
And here are the snails.
